about: Same five-step ladder as reviews.json (see its 'about'). {X} = the name he picks or types; {a}/{plural} = the kind of thing. 'against' marks the other side (the empty square on the card). · 25 Nov 2026 (the owner, after the content check): every way is a phrase the task's own model texts use (the Model and Guided/Sample steps), three alternatives per move, the moves in the models' order, so Basics teaches what the practice shows.
name: Article
how: An article in five sentences, as the model articles do: a question to hook the reader, your view, a moment you remember, what makes it special, and a last thought.
notebook: Write your article about {X} in five sentences, one per slot. Give it a title. Then check:
ticks: My title and first line make you want to read on.
I spoke to the reader directly.
I told a little story or gave an example.
My ending leaves the reader with a thought.

slots.job: hook the reader with a question

ways.t: If you could …, what would you choose?

slots.label: Hook

ways.t: For me, the answer has always been {X}.

slots.q: Which one tells a moment you remember?

ways.t: What makes the biggest difference, in my experience, is …
One of the key things I've learned is that …

slots.label: A moment

slots.q: Which one says what makes it special?

ways.t: What makes it so special is …
Apart from …, another thing that really stands out is …
One of the key things I love about {X} is …

slots.label: What makes it special

slots.job: leave the reader with a last thought
slots.q: Which one leaves a last thought?

ways.t: In short, there's something truly unforgettable about {X}.
Whether you agree or not, there's no denying that …
If you haven't … yet, make sure you do — you won't regret it.

slots.label: Last thought
